reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers read every German string again: start, 3 inputs plus the flyer, 10 exam texts, 8 redemittel, 2 speaking parts with 16 model turns, the writing task and model, the check lines, story and cliffhanger, and all explanations. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 12 reserve, 10 exam items, 8 check items and 4 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2/V1 order against accepted[]. For generated items we traced what the player builds. src/components/course-v2/content.js dictationItems: answer = line.de, and the audio is line.say || line.de (content.js l. 264/278, compiler.mjs l. 587). We graded answers with src/lib/lesson/check.js: punctuation is folded, and the typo allowance is Levenshtein 1. Exam blocks were checked against registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1 6×abc/3 options/2 plays/[32–53] words; h2 4×R/F/1 play/[29–47]; sp2, sp3, s2) and against rubrics sd1-sp2 / sd1-sp3 / sd1-s2 / course-micro / course-micro-sp (all resolve). Word counts were recomputed (h1: 42/41/38/41/37/39; h2: 31/31/35/30; flyer 47; model text 28). We also checked the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json (g.akkusativ chunkFrom a1.1-u04, productive a1.1-u06; g.kein a1.1-u06; g.praep-dativ chunk a1.1-u05). We ran the validator's own known-token machinery (knownForms + licensedForms) on every text and on story.cliffhanger. The rule cards were read against a1.1/rule-cards.json and the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json. The unit was compared with curriculum/a1-1.md §4, curriculum/a1-1.json and BLUEPRINT §2.8 (U4: H1, H2, Sp3, L2). Every price sum was recomputed (market 2,20 + 3,60 + 0,90 + 1,80 + 0,50 = 9,00 ✓; t1 3,50 + 2,00 = 5,50 ✓; 2 × 0,99 = 1,98 ✓; total spend ≈ 24 € of 50 € ✓). Every r1 finding was verified against the current file.

verdict: Not exit-ready, but close. The round-1 fixes are real. 25 of 26 findings are closed or closed for this unit (r1-F24 stays open as a detector class for the rule-smith). The sentence-building gaps, the false Stück rule and the butter contradiction are gone. The flyer is now read on its own. produkt-infos and the price echo are performed, and the exam texts are on length. The German is correct on every model surface, and du/Sie is right everywhere. One BLOCKER remains, and no earlier round could see it: an LS1 dictation generated from the input line ls1-l09 uses the written „1,19 Euro“ as its key, but the audio says only „eins neunzehn“. A learner who writes what they hear is graded WRONG. The other 10 findings are minors. That is more than the ≤ 5 logged MINOR allowed at exit, and 4 of them (F02, F03, F04, F05) are one-line data fixes.

findings.quote: ls1-l09 de „Und die Bananen? Die sind auch im Angebot. Ein Kilo kostet nur 1,19 Euro.“ · say „… Ein Kilo kostet nur eins neunzehn.“
findings.problem: The generator builds the dictation with answer = line.de and plays line.say (content.js dictationItems l. 182–203; playLine l. 264). The learner hears „eins neunzehn“, and the word „Euro“ is never spoken. A faithful transcription („… nur eins neunzehn“ or „… nur 1,19“) is therefore WRONG: check.js compares the whole sentence, the missing „Euro“ is 5 characters away and the typo allowance is 1, and normalizeDictation does not turn number words into digits. The generator has count 2 and two sources, so this item is built on every run. The answer cannot be derived from the audio.
findings.fix: Replace the source a1.1-u04-ls1-l09 with a line that has no `say` and no number, e.g. a1.1-u04-ls1-l06 („Und die Milch? Wir brauchen auch Milch. Die Milch ist auch billig, oder?“) or ls1-l04. Prices stay with numbers.dictation.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-06 (or a new ITM rule): a dictation.fromInput source line must not carry `say`, or its `say` must equal its `de` after digit folding. Failing fixture: a unit whose dictation source has de „… 1,19 Euro.“ and say „… eins neunzehn.“. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: tiles [die Butter / auch / ist / dort] · accepted includes „Dort ist die Butter auch.“ but not „Die Butter ist dort auch.“
findings.problem: The item accepts the mirror order with auch after the subject („Dort ist die Butter auch.“), but it rejects the same colloquial pattern with the subject in first position („Die Butter ist dort auch.“ – „Ja, die ist da auch.“). Both are spoken German of the same register, and a learner who builds one gets a red X while the other is green.
findings.fix: Add „Die Butter ist dort auch.“ with acceptedWhy „umgangssprachlich: auch nach dem Ortsadverb, das Verb bleibt auf Position 2“, or drop „Dort ist die Butter auch.“ so that both colloquial orders are treated alike.

findings.quote: „Priya sagt: „Die Eier sind billig.“ Wie viele Eier sind das?“ — options „ein Ei“ / „zwei oder mehr Eier“ / „kein Ei“
findings.problem: r1-F26 is only partly fixed. The key is still the only option that contains the stem's word „Eier“, so the item can be solved by matching strings, without reading die … sind as plural. The distractor „kein Ei“ also brings in kein (g.kein receptive from a1.1-u06) unglossed.
findings.fix: Make the plural cue the only route. Stem: „Welcher Satz sagt: mehr als ein Ei?“; options „Das Ei ist billig.“ / „Die Eier sind billig.“ / „Ein Ei ist billig.“ → key „Die Eier sind billig.“ (explanation: „Eier + sind: Plural.“).

findings.quote: h1-01 „40 Cent / 3,50 Euro / 5,50 Euro“ → 5,50 · h1-02 „100 / 200 / 300 Gramm“ → 300 · h1-03 „ein Ei / sechs Eier / zehn Eier“ → zehn
findings.problem: In the first three H1 items the options are in ascending order, and the key is each time the last option (c) and the largest value. The block's keys run c, c, c, a, a, b. ITM-03 passes because 3/2/1 is within ±1, but a test-wise learner who always picks the highest number scores 3 of 6, which is the habit SD1 Hören Teil 1 is built to defeat.
findings.fix: Reorder the options so that position and size do not give the key away, e.g. h1-02 „200 Gramm / 300 Gramm / 100 Gramm“ and h1-03 „zehn Eier / ein Ei / sechs Eier“. The block's keys should end up about 2/2/2.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-03: no run of ≥ 3 identical a/b/c keys within a block, and in a block with ≥ 3 numeric option sets the key must not always be the extreme value.

findings.quote: taskDe „… (20 bis 30 Wörter).“ · checklist „20 bis 30 Wörter“ · wordBandLearning [15, 25] · modelText 28 words
findings.problem: WritingTaskView.jsx l. 140 shows task.wordBandLearning || task.wordBand as the live target, so in Lern mode (modeDefault) the counter says „Ziel 15–25“, while the task line and the checklist on the same screen say 20–30. A learner who follows the instruction to 26–30 words sees the counter go off-target, and the model text (28 words) lies outside the band that is displayed.
findings.fix: Set wordBandLearning [20, 30] (or remove it). Alternatively, write „15 bis 25 Wörter“ in taskDe and the checklist and cut the model to ≤ 25 words.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-03: the word numbers in taskDe and checklist must equal the band the player displays (wordBandLearning when present, else wordBand), and modelText must lie inside that band.

findings.path: steps[3].texts t2, t3, t4, t6 (sd1.h1); steps[5].task.modelText
findings.quote: t3 „Hallo Priya, ich bin jetzt im Supermarkt. Brauchen wir Eier?“ – „Wir haben nur noch ein Ei.“ · t4 Priya: „Gut, dann ein Kilo Bananen, bitte.“ · t6 „dann kaufen wir vier Birnen“ · model „Zucker und Reis haben wir noch.“
findings.problem: The H1 dialogues retell the unit's Saturday with the same couple but with different facts. t3 repeats the Folge's „nur noch ein Ei“, yet Arjun is alone and on the phone, while in LS3 both of them buy the eggs together. In t4 Priya buys bananas (LS1: „Bananen brauchen wir nicht“) from the same market vendor (ensemble-a1-3), who in LS2 sold pears at 60 Cent each and now sells them at 2,10 €/kg. In t6 they buy four pears (LS2: three). In t2 Arjun buys 300 g of full-price cheese after „wir kaufen nur Angebote“. The LS6 model says rice is still at home, although in LS3 they had to buy rice. Each point is small, but together they blur the story that the unit builds.
findings.fix: Give LS4 speakers who are not the protagonists, as in the real SD1 (unnamed x.* extras or ensemble voices on both sides), or other cast members (e.g. Olena and Sophie in their WG). Otherwise mark the texts as another day. In the model text write „Zucker haben wir noch.“ (as in ls3-l10).
findings.proposedRule: Review check (CON class): a LS4 exam text spoken by the unit's protagonists must not contradict a fact set in the unit's scenes; the default is non-protagonist speakers in LS4.

findings.quote: „Heute ist Markt.“ · „Geld für eine Wohnung“ · „Geld für die Woche“ · „Am Montag sind wir wieder …“ · cliffhanger „Zu Hause liest Arjun die Zeitung. Dort steht eine Anzeige: „Wohnung in Leipzig: 2 Zimmer, Küche, Bad. Jetzt frei!““
findings.problem: Several words appear unglossed before their unit. „Markt“ is in no lexicon at all, although it is the LS2 setting (title „Auf dem Markt“, ls2-mo). „Wohnung“ belongs to u05, and „Woche“ and „Montag“ to u07. The cliffhanger, shown on the end screen in German only, has 7 unknown tokens in 27 words (Zeitung, which is in no lexicon, plus Anzeige, Wohnung, Zimmer, Küche, Bad, frei), about 74 % known. LEX-01 does not walk story.cliffhanger, so no gate sees this. „Dort steht eine Anzeige“ also refers to a newspaper with a place adverb.
findings.fix: Gloss Markt, Wohnung, Woche and Montag where they occur, and ask the lexicon owner to allocate lx.markt (A1 list) or keep it glossed. Cliffhanger: „Zu Hause liest Arjun die Zeitung. Darin steht eine Anzeige: …“, plus glosses or an English line for Zeitung, Anzeige, Zimmer, Küche, Bad and frei (their u05 words).
findings.proposedRule: LEX-01 walks story.cliffhanger (or SCHEMA gives the cliffhanger an `en` twin/glosses) at the same ≥ 95 % bar.

findings.quote: BLUEPRINT §2.8 U4 „H1, H2, Sp3, L2“ · curriculum/a1-1.md §4 „Lesen: Prospekt mit Angeboten (zwei Anzeigen vergleichen) (≈ 60 Wörter)“ · spec.situation „vergleichen Angebote im Prospekt“ · deviation null
findings.problem: Lesen Teil 2 (sd1.l2, choose between two ads) is planned for this unit, and its natural text is the unit's own flyer. The unit has one 47-word flyer, no two-ad comparison and no L2 block, and it logs no deviation. At the same time LS5 now opens with an sd1.sp2 round that appears neither in pruefungsfokus nor in the start chips, so the chip row and the syllabus page understate what the learner practises. Both Sp2 rounds also use the one topic „Einkaufen“, where the registry's Sp2 has two topics. Coverage is not at risk, because the plan places L2 in u05, u06, u08 and u12.
findings.fix: Record deviation.reason, e.g. „L2 ab u05; Sp2-Runde trägt cd.a1.produkt-infos (r1-F07)“, and drop 'vergleichen' from spec.situation. Alternatively, give LS1 a second short flyer (Markt vs. Supermarkt) with one a/b choice item. Give Sp2 round 2 a second topic (e.g. „Essen und Trinken“), or note the one-topic scaffold in the step's instructions.

findings.quote: „Unbestimmt heißt es ein (der, das) und eine (die).“ · table „unbestimmt | ein Apfel | ein Brot | eine Tomate“
findings.problem: Almost all of the unit's frames are accusative (brauchen, möchte, kaufen + object), and its chunk is „Ich möchte einen Apfel“ (ls2-l09, rm08, the Sp3 model). The card's rule is true only for the nominative and gives no warning. A learner who applies it to the unit's own sentence pattern writes ✗„Wir brauchen ein Käse / Ich möchte ein Apfel“, and rc.akkusativ then has to unteach this in u06 (§9.5: a simplification that has become false in context).
findings.fix: Rule-cards owner: label the row „unbestimmt (Nominativ)“ and add one line: „Achtung: Ich möchte einen Apfel. (maskulin nach möchte/brauchen → Einheit 6)“, keeping the card within the GRM-05 word limit.

findings.quote: „Guten Tag! Heute ist der Supermarkt nur bis 18 Uhr geöffnet. Morgen ist Sonntag, da ist alles zu.“
findings.problem: This is a register slip on an exam-text surface. A supermarket PA opens with „Liebe Kunden“ (as t7 and t10 do), not with „Guten Tag!“, and it announces its own closure („… ist unser Supermarkt geschlossen/zu“). „da ist alles zu“ is colloquial and vague (all shops? the whole store?).
findings.fix: „Liebe Kunden, heute ist unser Supermarkt nur bis 18 Uhr geöffnet. Morgen ist Sonntag, da ist der Supermarkt zu. Am Montag sind wir wieder von 8 bis 20 Uhr für Sie da. Danke und bis Montag!“ (36 words, inside [29–47]; add the „Liebe Kunden“ gloss).

findings.path: GRM-04 advisories: start.folge.lines[0], [5]; steps[1].input.lines[7], [8]; steps[3].texts[0].lines[4], texts[1].lines[3], [4]; steps[4].task.modelTurns[5]
findings.quote: det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel on „eine“ („für eine Wohnung“) · det.imperativ-du-ihr [shape fallback] on „300“ („300 Gramm, bitte.“) and „200“ („200 Gramm, bitte.“)
findings.problem: All 8 GRM-04 advisories are false positives, so there is no ceiling breach. Four repeat r1-F24, which is still open („bisschen“, „möchten“, and „macht … zusammen“, now 3×). Two false-positive classes are new: the Nullartikel detector fires on an indefinite article, and the imperative shape fallback reads a sentence-initial numeral as a verb. The second will fire on every shopping, time and number unit, and it hides real advisories in noise.
findings.fix: No unit change. Rule-smith: in det.imperativ-du-ihr, exclude digits and number words from the shape fallback; skip ein/eine/einen in det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel; and finish the r1-F24 stoplist („bisschen“, the möchte paradigm, „macht (das) zusammen“).
findings.proposedRule: GRM-04 detector fixtures: „300 Gramm, bitte.“ and „für eine Wohnung“ must produce no advisory; the test runs over all registered courses.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER / 0 MAJOR / every criterion ≥ 4 / ≤ 5 logged MINOR. Fixing F01 (one generator source id) lifts A to 4. F02, F03, F04 and F05 are one-line data fixes, and F06, F07 and F10 are small text edits in the unit. F09 belongs to the rule-cards owner and F11 to the rule-smith, so after the unit fixes the unit would carry at most 5 logged minors. Class findings for the rule-smith: F01, F04, F05, F06, F07, F11 (plus the open TXT-02 double tolerance from r1-F10).
